name: Energy Transfer 42-inch Fort Worth Basin to Carthage Pipeline (Barnett-Texoma Expansion Phases 1-3)

values.OtherEnglishNames: Barnett-Texoma Expansion; Fort Worth Basin to Carthage Pipeline

researcher_notes: Intrastate Texas line, so FERC silence is expected. EIA Aug 2026 release, sheet Historical Projects (1996-2024), Excel rows 405, 417 and 444, lists three Energy Transfer Barnett-Texoma Expansion phases, all completed, all 42-inch, intrastate: phase 1 new pipeline 97 mi, 600 MMcf/d, September 2006; phase 2 expansion 32 mi, 500 MMcf/d, December 2006; phase 3 expansion 135 mi, 700 MMcf/d, April 2007. Treated as one row. Length staged as 232 mi, the phase 1 plus phase 3 pipe, because the 32-mile phase 2 looks like the Carthage Loop, which a May 2008 trade press report says was completed in 2008 on the same line from Minden to Carthage; the EIA total of 264 mi and Energy Transfer's own 243 mile figure (from a March 2007 company release seen only in search results, the company site blocks automated fetches, so it is not cited) do not agree, so length is uncertain by about 10 percent. A June 2006 press report says the planned 42-inch Cleburne to Carthage line would cost $535 million and carry 1.6 Bcf/d, with XTO signed for 200 MMcf/d. Not the same as P3293 Texas Independence Pipeline (Maypearl to Henderson, 160 mi, completed 2009), P0265 Tiger (Carthage to Delhi) or the Southeast Bossier line (Farrar to Silsbee, 150 mi, separate project). No existing row has Cleburne to Carthage endpoints. Start year 2007 is the final phase completion. Route not researched: no official GIS found; RouteType unavailable until a map source is found. Owner style per entity_lookup: Energy Transfer LP on an alias hit. Capacity not staged because EIA gives per-phase incremental figures only. If the Carthage Loop is ruled its own row, it is 32 mi of 42-inch pipe (51 km, over the 25 km threshold) and would need a separate shard. Confidence medium: EIA is one origin, press reports corroborate the project but not the length.
